name: Dante I
def: Eight legged tethered walking robot sent into the crater of Mount Erebus in Antarctica, which failed a few metres into its descent.
body: Dante I was built by the Carnegie Mellon Field Robotics Center to show that a tethered walking machine could enter a volcanic crater too dangerous for people. It moved as a frame walker, sliding one frame of legs past the other, with power and communications carried on a tether from the crater rim. The tether failed shortly after it started down into the crater of Mount Erebus at the end of 1992, ending the descent after only a few metres.
facts: First attempt to send a walking robot into an active volcano
Tether failure ended the Mount Erebus descent
specs: Eight legs in two frames, moving one frame at a time
Supplied through a tether from the crater rim
